target_customer: Frontier AI labs, Fortune 100 companies and AI startups buying multimodal training data; originally developers who needed video search and editing APIs
problem: Progress on video, audio, image and world models is bottlenecked by high-quality multimodal data. At founding the problem was that developers found it hard to search and process large amounts of video.
business_model: Usage-based video AI API at launch, later custom dataset and environment sales to AI labs
product_category: Multimodal data and video AI infrastructure

founders.name: Mokshith Voodarla
education: UC Berkeley, B.S. Electrical Engineering and Computer Science
founders.background_notes: Computer vision work at the listed employers per the YC page.

founders.name: Abhinav (Abhi) Ayalur
education: UC Berkeley, B.S. Electrical Engineering and Computer Science
founders.background_notes: Computer vision, data analysis and API development per the YC page.

technical_complexity.rationale: Sieve claimed it could process 24 hours of video in under 10 minutes using filtering, parallelization and interpolation, which needs real computer vision and infrastructure work for a two person team.

defensibility.rationale: A pluggable video API sat on top of open models and cloud compute, so it was easy to copy. Defensibility came later from data sourcing scale and lab relationships, which the sources only describe as company claims.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No source shows an incumbent copying or buying Sieve. The company instead pivoted away from video APIs toward datasets, announced in its March 2026 reintroduction post.

market_need_then: Developers wanted to search and edit video with a few API calls, as the Launch HN thread of early 2022 framed it. Spend and complaint data were not found.

branding.domain_note: Used sievedata.com for years; sievedata.com now redirects to sieve.ai (a third-party guide and the redirect seen on fetch). Exact date of the move not found.

identity.logo: Not described in any source found
identity.visual_style: Developer-tool style with a Notion-hosted docs and blog presence

rebrands.from: Video AI API positioning on sievedata.com
rebrands.why: Company says it moved from video APIs to end-to-end multimodal datasets; this was a repositioning and domain move, not a name change.

branding.community_and_virality: A Product Hunt launch in January 2022 and a Launch HN thread are the only community signals found.

brand_strength.rationale: Real-word name shared with unrelated products such as usesieve.com, with little press about the brand itself.

pivots.from: Pluggable video search, understanding and editing APIs
pivots.to: Multimodal datasets and environments for frontier AI labs
pivots.why: Stated in the company's Reintroducing Sieve post; the date comes from a third-party summary of that post.

outcome_analysis: Sieve launched in early 2022 with a developer video API and raised an announced seed of about four million dollars in November 2022. Its YC page now shows 34 people and a repositioning toward data for frontier labs, which suggests the video API market was too thin and the team found demand in training data. Customer claims are the company's own and revenue is not public, so the success of the pivot is unverified.
notes: The company blog post titled Sieve's Video AI API Beta and ~$4M Raise (14 Nov 2022) is cited on the YC page; its host chicken.sievedata.com did not resolve here, so the amount is confirmed by YC page plus Seedtable only, and investors are unknown. CB Insights reports a $0.5M convertible note in April 2025 with YC; seen in one aggregator only, so unverified and not recorded. Total raised figures conflict across aggregators ($4.1M to $12M). Competitor list is short because pre-batch dated sources for Google or AWS video APIs were not found.
